competencies.text: Describe typhoons, floods, landslides, storm surges, and heat waves.

days.title: Weather Hazards in the Philippines
days.content:
Learning Target

By the end of today's lesson, you will be able to describe the major hydrometeorological hazards affecting the Philippines — typhoons, floods, landslides, storm surges, and heat waves — and explain their causes, warning signs, and effects.

What Are Hydrometeorological Hazards?

Hydrometeorological hazards are natural hazards caused by atmospheric, oceanic, or hydrological processes. The Philippines is particularly vulnerable because of:

  • Location in the typhoon belt (Western Pacific)
  • Warm ocean waters (fuel for typhoons)
  • An archipelago with long coastlines
  • Mountainous terrain prone to landslides
  • Many low-lying coastal communities

Typhoons (Tropical Cyclones)

A typhoon is a powerful, rotating storm system that forms over warm ocean waters (at least 26.5 degrees Celsius). It has:

  • Eye — calm center with lowest pressure
  • Eyewall — strongest winds and heaviest rain
  • Spiral rain bands — outer bands causing widespread rain

PAGASA Tropical Cyclone Wind Signals:

SignalWind SpeedExpected Impact
Signal No. 139–61 km/hVery light damage; some trees sway
Signal No. 262–88 km/hLight to moderate damage; some trees broken
Signal No. 389–117 km/hModerate to heavy damage; many trees down
Signal No. 4118–184 km/hHeavy to very heavy damage; widespread destruction
Signal No. 5185+ km/hExtreme damage; catastrophic

About 20 tropical cyclones enter Philippine waters each year; 8–9 make landfall.

Floods

A flood is the overflow of water onto normally dry land. Types:

TypeCause
Riverine floodRivers overflow from heavy rain
Flash floodSudden, fast-rising water — common in mountain areas
Urban floodDrainage systems overwhelmed; poor urban planning
Coastal floodStorm surges or sea-level rise

Main causes: heavy rainfall, deforestation, clogged drainage, and urbanization.

Landslides

A landslide is the sudden downward movement of rock, soil, and debris. Common triggers:

  • Heavy rainfall (saturates soil)
  • Earthquakes
  • Volcanic eruptions
  • Deforestation and mining (weaken slopes)
  • Steep terrain and unstable geology

Warning signs: cracks in the ground, tilting trees or posts, unusual water seepage, rumbling sounds.

Storm Surges

A storm surge is the abnormal rise of sea level near the coast, caused by a typhoon's strong winds and low pressure. It can:

  • Reach 5–7 meters in extreme cases (like Yolanda/Haiyan in 2013)
  • Flood coastal communities within minutes
  • Cause most typhoon deaths when combined with high tide

Most vulnerable: coastal barangays, especially in Eastern Visayas and Bicol.

Heat Waves

A heat wave is a prolonged period of abnormally high temperatures, often combined with high humidity. In the Philippines:

  • Heat index (the feels like temperature) can reach danger levels (41–54 degrees Celsius)
  • DOH and PAGASA issue heat advisories
  • Vulnerable: elderly, children, outdoor workers, and those with health conditions

Heat index categories:

Heat IndexCategoryEffect
27–32 CCautionFatigue possible with prolonged exposure
33–41 CExtreme CautionHeat cramps and heat exhaustion possible
42–51 CDangerHeat cramps, exhaustion likely; heat stroke possible
52 C+Extreme DangerHeat stroke imminent

The Role of PAGASA

PAGASA monitors and warns about:

  • Typhoons and tropical cyclones
  • Floods and rainfall
  • Storm surges
  • Heat index
  • El Nino and La Nina events

PAGASA issues bulletins every 3–6 hours during active weather events.

Preparedness Basics

  • Monitor PAGASA updates before, during, and after storms.
  • Prepare a Go Bag with water, food, flashlight, radio, medicines, and important documents.
  • Know your evacuation center and routes.
  • Secure loose objects; reinforce roofs and windows.
  • Never cross flooded roads or wade in floodwater.
  • Follow local government advisories on preemptive evacuation.

Quick Check

  • How many tropical cyclones enter Philippine waters each year? (Answer: about 20)
  • What causes a storm surge? (Answer: a typhoon's strong winds and low pressure pushing sea water onto the coast)
  • Which agency issues typhoon warnings in the Philippines? (Answer: PAGASA)

days.title: Match Game — Weather Hazards
days.content:
Activity 1 — Match the Pairs

Match each hydrometeorological hazard or concept to its correct description. There are 8 pairs.

match.right: Powerful rotating storm that forms over warm ocean waters (at least 26.5 C)
Calm center with the lowest pressure
Ring around the eye with the strongest winds and heaviest rain
Abnormal rise of sea level near the coast, caused by typhoon winds and low pressure
Sudden, fast-rising water — common in mountain areas after heavy rain
Sudden downward movement of rock, soil, and debris on a slope
The feels like temperature combining heat and humidity
Agency that monitors typhoons, floods, storm surges, and heat index

days.title: Scenario Challenge — Storm Preparedness
days.content:
Activity 2 — Scenario Challenge

Read each scenario and choose the best reasoning. There are 5 scenarios.

scenario.text: PAGASA raises Signal No. 3 in your province. What does this mean for residents?

choices.label: A) Winds of 89–117 km/h are expected — moderate to heavy damage; prepare for possible evacuation
B) It is just a light rain warning
C) The typhoon has already passed
D) Nothing will happen

scenario.text: A coastal barangay is warned of a possible 5-meter storm surge. What should residents do?

choices.label: A) Evacuate to higher ground or designated evacuation centers immediately
B) Stay home and wait it out
C) Go to the beach to watch the waves
D) Move to the second floor of their house

scenario.text: After three days of continuous heavy rain, you notice cracks appearing on a hillside near your house. What should you do?

choices.label: A) Evacuate immediately — cracks are a warning sign of an impending landslide
B) Ignore them — they are normal
C) Fill the cracks with soil
D) Take pictures only

scenario.text: A river near your barangay is rising fast after hours of rain. What is the SAFEST action?

choices.label: A) Move to higher ground and avoid crossing flooded areas
B) Try to cross the river to check on neighbors
C) Wait until the water reaches your house
D) Swim across

scenario.text: PAGASA reports a heat index of 48 C in your area. What should outdoor workers do?

choices.label: A) Avoid prolonged exposure, drink plenty of water, and take breaks in the shade — heat stroke is possible
B) Work longer hours to finish quickly
C) Wear thick clothing
D) Ignore it — heat index doesn't matter

days.title: Formative Check — Escape the Weather Lab
days.content:
Formative Check — Escape the Weather Lab

You have 3 lives and 6 keys to unlock. You need 75% (5 of 6) to pass.

escape.text: About how many tropical cyclones enter Philippine waters each year?

choices.label: A) About 20
B) About 3
C) About 50
D) About 100
A) A typhoon's strong winds and low pressure pushing sea water onto the coast
B) Underwater earthquakes
C) Lunar tides only
D) Volcanic eruptions

escape.text: Which of the following is the STRONGEST part of a typhoon?

choices.label: A) The eyewall
B) The eye
C) The outer rain bands
D) The tail
A) The feels like temperature combining heat and humidity
B) The actual air temperature
C) The temperature of the ocean
D) The temperature inside the house

escape.text: Which agency issues typhoon warnings and heat advisories in the Philippines?

choices.label: A) PAGASA
B) PHIVOLCS
C) DENR
D) DOH only

escape.text: What should you do if caught in a flood?

choices.label: A) Move to higher ground immediately; never attempt to cross flooded roads
B) Try to drive through the flood
C) Wade through the water
D) Wait for the water to reach you
